title: Netstrings (1997)
summary: Netstrings is a simple data format protocol created by D.J. Bernstein in 1997 that encodes messages as length-prefixed strings (e.g., '5:hello,') for reliable binary data transmission, avoiding delimiter collision issues common in other formats.
problem_solved: Provides a self-delimiting binary-safe data format that eliminates ambiguity in parsing without requiring escape sequences or complex delimiters.
why_valuable: Its elegant simplicity (25+ years old) makes it one of the cleanest solutions for transmitting length-tagged data with guaranteed unambiguous parsing boundaries.
